summary: We created a game to help inspire young astronauts in interplanetary survival. Through a survival strategy game, "Red Harvest," we implemented real data from NASA and true botanical facts about nutrition and soil condition to mimic how survival on Mars could play out. Since the landing zones are direct copies of Martian terrain, the soil conditions come from NASA data, crop mutations are generated randomly based on solar activity, weather comes from NASA-reported data, a person playing our game could only succeed by following rules of real life. By creating a game that closely mimics real world behavior, we hope to inspire young astronauts by teaching them not through lectures but through their own curiosity.
details:
Our project is a game that helps young astronauts learn the basics behind botany in Mars through a simulation. We use NASA's data for solar activity, soil content, weather conditions, and hydrogen as well as true botanical information regarding nutrition, time for maturity, and a Mendellian gene system to add elements of randomness to survival.

We intend for our project to help young scholars learn more through a fun game rather than have another boring tool.

We used Cursor, Claude Design, and Codex to frame a large portion of our code. We primarily worked in JavaScript, deploying our project with Node.js.

We first wanted to pursue a Roblox game, since the 3D element would add a nice interactivity to our project, but time constraints limited us to working purely in the web. Furthermore, we had to trim our project's scope from a general Martian colonization to just Martian survival since the timespan would be too large for a simple demo. There were many unique features that mentors advised us to trim for simplicity, like a tech tree, advanced genetic crosses, more realistic soil washing, and more.

We aimed to be creative through our perspectives. We are students who grew up with survival games on CoolMathGames, and making one enjoyable to play was our most exciting task of the weekend.
